name: Seychelles Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Gébert, Alain & Annie Risler. 2019. A dictionary and grammar of Seychellois Sign Language / Diksyoner e gramer Lalang Siny Seselwa / Dictionnaire et grammaire de la Langue des Signes Seychelloise, Vol. 1. Victoria: APHI Seychelles. 365 pp. (trilingual Kreol/French/English)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Part one 'How do we sign?' (English, book pp. 65-72 = PDF pp. 67-74) describes sign 'pronunciation' as three manual parameters (42 handshapes, movement, location) plus non-manual parameters (facial expression, head, mouth/labialization, gaze, eyebrows, posture); the grammar part (pp. 305-330) notes aspectual intensification via movement dynamics and breath. No mention of stress, accent, prosody or rhythm anywhere in the 365 pages (a full-text search for stress/accent extracted text, en/fr/crs).
